Shooting In Charleston Reignites Debate About The Confederate Flag

I read about this today. Some Americans view the CSA flag as racist, because the American Civil War was fought over slavery (and between the states which sided on the different sides of the issue). But an argument can be made that the flag may represent the "states vs. Feds" argument (this issue still sticks with contemporary issues like the Affordable Health Care Act, speed limits, firearms ownership, capital punishment, et al.).

So the whole thing boils down to whether or not the people who vote see the flag as "just racist / pro Jim Crow" or as something more. Me, I'm a Civil War enthusiast, so I don't really care. Declaring the CSA flag as racist also makes watching / fapping to Daisy Dukes on the Dukes of Hazzard awkward.

At the end of the day, it is the flag of a regime that formed for the primary purpose of defending an economic way of life that depended on slavery (and who took threats against slavery very seriously to the point of secession). The heritage/culture/state's rights/etc... narrative was formed during and after the war to justify the war in lights other than the "peculiar institution" of slavery.

Oh yeah Mosin91 - the CSA unfortunately had to depend on a slave labor economy to work (much like the Roman Empire); however, you should remember that the "States Rights" vs "'dem Feds" argument also applies to: health care, firearms, abortion, taxation (sales, income, etc.), marriage (this one currently going through SCOTUS for correct classification with the IRS and state tax filings each year).

Yeah. Race-based slavery is generally considered to be bad, but a flag's a flag. With technology to IFF combatants with facial, olfactory, and (possibly) biometric recognition, flags are pretty meaningless outside of the parade ground or civic celebrations.

However these numbers are just estimated by me and it is actually hard to figure them out for power lifters as they have a very different body shape from most other humans. They have very strong core muscles which makes them often appear fatter than they are.

But a lot of them are still fatter than what I would usually like in normal humans. But this is necessary for their sport as you can simply get stronger when you eat a little bit more than you would need to. Also having some excess fat can be very helpful for the lifts. So the difference here compared to regular fatties is that the power lifters don't get fat because they lack discipline but because they need this to reach their goal for which they train with a lot of discipline.
